messages:
Alex: Quick follow-up from the RFC — proposal for attaching 'kernel tags' to quant profiles so runtime can pick FP8/INT8/4bit kernels without branching too much.
Maya: +1, can you sketch what a tag looks like? e.g., opset-level or layer-level?
Alex: opset-level mostly, with optional per-layer override. tag example: 'fp8_attn_v2|int8_mm_v1|fallback_4bit'
Tariq: Concern: memory layout differences — if we flip kernels mid-sequence we might need KV reformat which is expensive.
Sophie: Right — that was the big perf risk. Suggest we allow a 'gradual switch' window: do kernel switch at block boundaries only.
Alex: Agreed. Also thinking packaging quant profiles as immutable artifacts with semantic versioning. Runtime resolves by model+profile_id.
Maya: That helps ops. How will we express quality constraints? We need min_quality or degradation_budget in the profile.
Alex: Exactly — add fields: min_quality (float), max_p99_latency_ms, fallback_order list.
Ken: Can you paste a sample profile payload?
Alex: 
```json
{
  "profile_id": "qprof-2026-07-01-a",
  "model": "redwood-7b",
  "tags": ["fp8_attn_v2","int8_mm_v1"],
  "min_quality": 0.98,
  "degradation_budget": 0.02,
  "fallback_order": ["int8_mm_v1","4bit_mm_v2"],
  "canary_traffic_pct": 2
}
```
Maya: Nice. Runtime needs to surface why it chose a fallback — we should emit telemetry: chosen_tag, reason, quality_delta, sample_prompt_id.
Tariq: Also track per-tenant quality escrow so customers with stricter SLAs aren't auto-downgraded.
Sophie: Ops question — how do we avoid memory fragmentation when switching kernels? Need a pre-allocated slab per kernel or a shared pool with quick reclaim.
Alex: Option A: pre-allocate small scratch slabs for each supported kernel on startup. Option B: evict lesser-used caches dynamically.
Ken: Option A costs memory for every model instance. Option B risks latency spikes from allocs.
Maya: Maybe hybrid: pre-allocate only for the most likely pair (default tag + first fallback) and lazy allocate others.
Tariq: For canaries: run offline eval that measures NLL delta and a small distributed canary with live traffic 1-2% and alert if delta > min_quality.
Sophie: Regarding API — propose request header "X-Quant-Profile" with profile_id to pin, and runtime will reject if incompatible.
Alex: Also add a 'soft_pin' mode where runtime attempts but will fallback automatically under pressure.
Ken: What about per-token fallback (e.g., degrade to int8 for next tokens only)? Is that feasible?
Tariq: We discussed token-level switching earlier — high complexity. If we do it, must keep KV cache formats compatible or convert on switch.
Maya: Another approach: prefix-aware routing. If prefix is in cache and tagged fp8, continue same kernel; new tokens can be generated on fallback kernel but aligners are tricky.
Sophie: Ops runbook: when we see quality_budget burn >50% in 5m, rollback to previous profile and trigger eval-run. Add page for engineers.
Alex: Action items: (1) Draft profile schema PR, (2) prototype kernel-tag registry in runtime, (3) write canary harness for perf+quality, (4) ops rollback runbook.
Maya: I'll take (1) and (3). Ken takes (2). Tariq/Sophie will draft the runbook.
Ken: timeline? aim for an internal canary in 3 weeks.
Alex: Sounds good. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
quant-bot: Note: Created ticket INFR-5421 for kernel registry work.
Maya: Added eq tests to INFR-5421, linking evals repo.
Ken: ping @Alex for API changes once schema PR is up.
Sophie: small nit – ensure profile artifacts are signed so private deployments can verify.
Alex: Good call. We'll add signature and checksum fields.
Maya: End-to-end checklist in the ticket please.
Alex: Will do — closing thread for now.
